}}'''Katherine Mary Blundell''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|OBE}} is a [[professor]] of [[astrophysics]] at the [[University of Oxford]] and a [[wikt:supernumerary|supernumerary]] [[research fellow]] at [[St John's College, Oxford]].<ref name=sjc>{{cite web|url=https://www.sjc.ox.ac.uk/discover/people/professor-katherine-blundell|website=sjc.ox.ac.uk|title=Professor Katherine Blundell OBE Supernumerary Research Fellow in Astrophysics}}</ref> Previously, she held a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]],{{when|date=February 2018}} and [[fellow]]ships from the [[Royal Commission for the Exhibition of 1851]] and [[Balliol College, Oxford]].<ref name=ox>{{cite web|url=http://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/contacts/people/blundell|website=physics.ox.ac.uk|title=Katherine Blundell Professor of Astrophysics}}</ref><ref name="Blundell1996">{{cite journal|last1=Blundell|first1=K. M.|title=Evidence for widely separated primary and secondary hotspots in 3C 171|journal=[[Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society]]|volume=283|issue=2|year=1996|pages=538–542|issn=0035-8711|doi=10.1093/mnras/283.2.538|bibcode=1996MNRAS.283..538B|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Education==
Blundell was educated at the [[University of Cambridge]]<ref name=iwd>{{cite web|first=Laurie|last=Winkless|author-link=Laurie Winkless|year=2016|title=International Womens Day 2016: Life and research with Katherine Blundell|url=https://blogs.royalsociety.org/inside-science/2016/03/01/iwd2016-life-and-research-with-katherine-blundell/|website=blogs.royalsociety.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419061106/https://blogs.royalsociety.org/inside-science/2016/03/01/iwd2016-life-and-research-with-katherine-blundell/|archive-date=2016-04-19|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}}</ref> where she was awarded a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree {{when|date=February 2018}} followed by a [[PhD]] in 1995 for research on [[Radio galaxy|radio galaxies]] and [[quasar]]s.<ref name=blundellphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=http://idiscover.lib.cam.ac.uk/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=44CAM_ALMA21429631420003606&context=L&vid=44CAM_PROD&search_scope=SCOP_CAM_ALL&tab=cam_lib_coll&lang=en_US|title=Asymmetries in radio galaxies and quasars|first= Katherine Mary|last=Blundell|date=1995|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.338069}}|website=lib.cam.ac.uk|oclc=53602207}}</ref><ref name=ard>{{cite web|first=Ard|last=Louis|author-link=Ard Louis|year=2016|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RBusi0bdzGE|website=youtube.com|publisher=[[YouTube]]|title=Katherine Blundell: Academic Journey}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Blundell's research<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref> investigates the physics of active galaxies – such as [[quasar]]s. She also studies objects in the [[Milky Way]] such as [[microquasar]]s which produce [[astrophysical jet]]s of [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] that emit [[radio wave]]s and move at speeds close to the [[speed of light]].<ref name=sjc/>

Blundell is founder of the Global Jet Watch (GJW) project,<ref name=gjw>{{cite web|url=https://www.globaljetwatch.net|website=globaljetwatch.net|title=Global Jet Watch Home}}</ref> which records [[spectroscopic|spectroscopic measurements]] of microquasars such as [[SS 433]].<ref name="BlundellBowler2004">{{cite journal|last1=Blundell|first1=Katherine M.|last2=Bowler|first2=Michael G.|title=Symmetry in the Changing Jets of SS 433 and Its True Distance from Us|journal=[[The Astrophysical Journal]]|volume=616|issue=2|year=2004|pages=L159–L162|issn=0004-637X|doi=10.1086/426542|arxiv=astro-ph/0410456|bibcode=2004ApJ...616L.159B|s2cid=11213274 }}</ref><ref name=jeffphd>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|url=https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:b9f5657b-a122-464f-8c55-db349ba74c4c|title=The remarkable outflows from the galactic microquasar SS433|first= Robert|last=Jeffrey|date=2016|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.730205}}|website=ora.ox.ac.uk}} {{free access}}</ref> The project uses five [[Ritchey–Chrétien telescope]]s separated in [[longitude]] around the [[Earth]] so that at any time at least one of them is in night-time. Two of the telescopes are located in Australia ([[Western Australia]] and [[New South Wales]]), with one each in [[India]], [[South Africa]] and [[Chile]].<ref name=gjw/>

Blundell's work has been funded by the [[Science and Technology Facilities Council]] (STFC),<ref name=gtr>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180205125312/http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/B7ABFCFB-4750-45AC-9312-B146E0E67206|archive-date=2018-02-05|url=http://gtr.rcuk.ac.uk/person/B7ABFCFB-4750-45AC-9312-B146E0E67206|title=UK Government grants awarded to Katherine Blundell|website=rcuk.ac.uk|publisher=[[Research Councils UK]]|author=Anon|year=2018|location=Swindon}}</ref> the [[Royal Society]]<ref name=iwd/> and the [[Royal Commission for the Exhibition of 1851]]. Her collaborators have included [[Steven Balbus]],<ref name=gtr/> [[Steven Rawlings]],<ref name=nature>{{cite journal|last1=Blundell|first1=Katherine M.|last2=Rawlings|first2=Steve|title=The inevitable youthfulness of known high-redshift radio galaxies|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|arxiv=astro-ph/9905333|volume=399|issue=6734|year=1999|pages=330–332|issn=0028-0836|doi=10.1038/20612|bibcode=1999Natur.399..330B|s2cid=4430153 }} {{closed access}}</ref> [[Roger Davies (astrophysicist)|Roger Llewelyn Davies]],<ref name=gtr/> [[Stephen Blundell]]<ref name=thermal/> and [[Fraser Armstrong (professor)|Fraser A. Armstrong]].<ref name=oil/><ref name=hep>{{cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/K.M.Blundell.1|website=inspirehep.net|publisher=[[INSPIRE-HEP]]|title=Blundell, Katherine Mary - Profile}}</ref>

Blundell is the author or co-author of several books, including ''Black Holes : A Very Short Introduction'',<ref name=vsi>{{Cite book|title=Black holes : A Very Short Introduction|last=Blundell|first=Katherine|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|year=2015|isbn=9780199602667|doi=10.1093/actrade/9780199602667.001.0001 |edition=1st|location=Oxford|oclc=932859524}}</ref> ''Concepts in Thermal Physics''<ref name=thermal>{{Cite book|title=Concepts in thermal physics|last1=Blundell|first1=Stephen J.|last2=Blundell|first2=Katherine M.|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|year=2010|isbn=9780199562107|edition=2nd|location=Oxford|oclc=607907330|doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199562091.001.0001 }}</ref> and ''Energy... beyond Oil''.<ref name=oil>{{Cite book|title=Energy... beyond oil|date=2007|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|first1=Fraser|last1=Armstrong|first2=Katherine |last2=Blundell|isbn=9780199209965|location=Oxford|oclc=314220853}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Blundell is married to [[Stephen Blundell]].

==Honours and awards==
Blundell was appointed [[Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2017 Birthday Honours]] for services to astronomy and the education of young people.<ref name=obe>{{cite web|url=https://www.thegazette.co.uk/notice/2804227|website=thegazette.co.uk|publisher=[[The London Gazette]]|title=Professor Katherine Mary BLUNDELL: Order of the British Empire|author=Anon|year=2017}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]] in Astrophysics in 2005, the [[Rosalind Franklin Award]] from the [[Royal Society]] in 2010, the [[Lawrence Bragg Medal and Prize]] from the [[Institute of Physics]] (IOP) in 2012 and the [[George Darwin Lectureship]] from the [[Royal Astronomical Society]] (RAS) in 2015.<ref name=sjc/><ref name=ox/> In 2026, the [[main belt asteroid]] 1995 XC was named [[31006 Katherine|(31006) Katherine]] after her.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Names of Minor Planets published on 2026 March 16 |url=https://theasteroidnews.com/New-Names-of-Minor-Planets-published-on-2026-March-16.html |access-date=2026-10-30 |website=The Asteroid News |language=en}}</ref>
